JUDGMENT
By this common order, Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 375/2007 and 385/2007 shall be decided.

2. Both the miscellaneous appeals have been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act against the award dated 04/01/2007 passed by Additional Judge to the Court of Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Shivpuri in MACC No. 20/2006.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11512 2 MA-375-2007 3.
Impugned award was passed by Hon'ble Judge who has a roster of hearing miscellaneous appeals.
By order dated 16/09/2025, Co-ordinate Bench of this Court had directed to list this case before another Bench.
Accordingly, by order of Hon'ble the Chief Justice, these two cases have been listed before this Court.

1 4.
M.A. No. 375/2007 has been filed by Anand Jain, who was the driver and owner of offending TVS motorcycle, and Kishore has filed M.A. No. 385/2007 as claimant.
5. The facts necessary for disposal of present appeals, in short, are that on 08/03/2005 at about 6:00 PM, claimant was going to offer prayer in Manshapurn Hanuman Mandir .

When he reached near Thakur Baba ki Tek , it was alleged that driver/owner, namely Anand Jain, by driving the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the claimant, as a result he fell unconscious on the spot.
Crime No. 108/2005 was registered against Anand Jain for offenses under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC.
Claimant had suffered injuries resulting in 19 stitches on his head.
Accordingly, he filed a claim petition for award of compensation of Rs. 8,30,000/-.
6. Anand Jain filed his written statement and claimed that no accident had taken place.
7. Respondent No. 2 remained ex-parte and no written statement was filed.
8. The Claims Tribunal, after framing issues and recording evidence, partially allowed the claim petition and awarded Rs. 18,500/- by way of compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11512 3 MA-375-2007 9.
Challenging the award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for Anand Jain (appellant in M.A. No. 375/2007) that Anand Jain was falsely implicated.
He was neither the owner of motorcycle nor he was driving the motorcycle.
It is further submitted that even the accident did not take place with the motorcycle of Anand Jain.
10. On the contrary, counsel for claimant, who is appellant in M.A. No. 385/2007, has submitted that claimant had suffered injury on his head which was treated by giving 19 stitches

, therefore,
compensation of Rs. 18,500/- is on the lower side.

11. Considered the submissions made by counsel for parties.
12.
The moot question for consideration is as to whether the accident was caused by Anand Jain by driving the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner or not?
13. Record of the Claims Tribunal has been received in M.A. No. 385/2007.
From the record, it is clear that Dehati Nalishi (Exhibit P-2) was lodged by one stranger, namely Amritlal Jatav, to the effect that he was going towards his house.
As soon as he reached in front of the house of Mahesh Pandey, one cyclist was going ahead of him.

At that time, one person came from the side of Satanwada and by driving the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the cyclist from front, as a result, the unknown cyclist fell on the ground and suffered injury on his head.
Accident was caused by Anand Jain, resident of Satnawada.

This Dehati Nalishi was lodged on 08/03/2005 at 19:10, whereas accident took place on 08/03/2005 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11512 4 MA-375-2007 at 18:45.

Thus, it is clear that within 25 minutes of accident, Dehati Nalishi (Exhibit P-2) was lodged by a stranger, and in that Dehati Nalishi , name of Anand Jain vs Kishor on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78992189/
2 the driver of offending motorcycle was specifically disclosed as Anand Jain, resident of Satnawada.
14. Although it is submitted by counsel for appellant Anand Jain that motorcycle number was not mentioned in Dehati Nalishi , but said submission is misconceived and has no relevance.
It is specifically mentioned in the Dehati Nalishi that the motorcycle was not carrying any registration number on it.

Even otherwise, identification of the motorcycle is required for insurance purposes,
but the primary allegations are against the driver.

In the present case, name of the driver, i.e.,
Anand Jain was specifically mentioned in the Dehati Nalishi lodged within 30 minutes of the accident and that too by a stranger.

15. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that the accident was caused by appellant Anand Jain by driving the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.

16. Appellant/Claimant Kishore Vaishnav has filed discharge ticket (Exhibit P-10C), according to which claimant remained hospitalized in J.A. Group of Hospitals, Gwalior from 09/03/2005 to 28/03/2005.
He was given 19 stitches for the treatment of his head injury.
17. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the total compensation amount of Rs. 18,500/- is on the lower side.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11512 5 MA-375-2007
Accordingly, it is enhanced by a further sum of Rs. 21,500/- , and it is held that claimant Kishore Vaishnav is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs. 40,000/-.
18. Other conditions of the award will remain the same.

19. With aforesaid modification, award dated 04/01/2007 passed by Additional Judge to the Court of Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Shivpuri in MACC No.
20/2006 is hereby affirmed.
